<STRUCT_0001>
At this point we have developed enough machinery to prove that residual
gerbes (when they exist) are gerbes.

Let <MATH_0001> be a reduced, locally Noetherian algebraic stack
such that <MATH_0002> is a singleton. Then <MATH_0003> is a gerbe
over a reduced, locally Noetherian algebraic space <MATH_0004> with <MATH_0005> a
singleton.

By
Properties of Stacks, Lemma <REF_0001>
there exists a surjective, flat, locally finitely presented morphism
<MATH_0001> where <MATH_0002> is a field.
Then <MATH_0003>
is representable by algebraic spaces and
locally of finite type (as a base change of
<MATH_0004>, see
Lemmas <REF_0002> and <REF_0003>).
Therefore it is locally of finite presentation, see
Morphisms of Spaces, Lemma
<REF_0004>.
Of course it is also flat as <MATH_0005> is a field. Hence we may apply
Lemmas <REF_0005> and
<REF_0006>
to see that <MATH_0006> is flat and
locally of finite presentation. We conclude that <MATH_0007>
is a gerbe by
Proposition <REF_0007>.
Let <MATH_0008> be a morphism to an algebraic space such
that <MATH_0009> is a gerbe over <MATH_0010>. Then <MATH_0011> is surjective, flat, and
locally of finite presentation by
Lemma <REF_0008>.
Hence <MATH_0012> is surjective, flat, and locally of finite
presentation as a composition, see
Properties of Stacks,
Lemma <REF_0009>
and
Lemmas <REF_0010> and
<REF_0011>.
Hence by
Properties of Stacks, Lemma <REF_0012>
we see that <MATH_0013> is a singleton and that <MATH_0014> is locally Noetherian
and reduced.
